title: Founders, Inc.
blurb: Fort Mason Center Landmark Building C, 2 Marina Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94123

params.clue: Your first stop is right beside you: land on the long cream warehouse with the red roof at the foot of Fort Mason, where a founder campus builds the next big startups.
params.fact: Founders, Inc. builds startups inside the old Army port at Fort Mason, which shipped more than 1.65 million soldiers and 23 million tons of cargo to the Pacific.

params.clue: Every founder needs fuel. Fly east along the waterfront to Fisherman's Wharf and land outside the only burger stand of a famous California chain inside the city, on Jefferson Street.
params.fact: It is the only In-N-Out in San Francisco, open since September 20, 2001, and it has no drive-thru.

title: Coit Tower
blurb: 1 Telegraph Hill Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94133

params.clue: Fed and ready? Look east-southeast to the slim fluted column crowning Telegraph Hill and land on its very top.
params.fact: Despite the popular story, Coit Tower was not designed to look like a fire hose nozzle; the resemblance is a coincidence.

title: Corgi
blurb: 222 Sutter St (cafe and office entrance at 9 Claude Ln), San Francisco, CA 94108

params.clue: From the hilltop, fly south into the Financial District and find the YC startup whose cafe never closes, under its office on tiny Claude Lane just off Sutter Street.
params.fact: Founded in 2024, Corgi was valued at $2.6 billion by June 2026, and the cafe under its office never closes.

params.clue: Coffee in hand, fly northeast to the foot of Market Street, where a clock tower has greeted ferry riders since 1898.
params.fact: Until the bridges opened in the 1930s, it was the second busiest transit terminal in the world after London's Charing Cross.

params.clue: Turn due west and find the white pointed tower that has defined the skyline since 1972; thread the ring around its spire.
params.fact: A grove of redwoods brought from the Santa Cruz Mountains grows at its foot, with a bronze jumping frog honoring Mark Twain.

params.clue: The pyramid was the city's tallest building until 2017. Fly southeast to the tower that took the title and land on its crown.
params.fact: Its top floors hold Day for Night, an artwork by Jim Campbell made of 11,000 LED lights that glows over the city at night.

params.clue: From the top of the city, glide south-southeast toward the ballpark: on Townsend Street a three-story brick building houses the venture firm whose nickname hides a number between two letters.
params.fact: The nickname a16z counts the 16 letters between the a of Andreessen and the z of Horowitz.

params.clue: Term sheet in hand, fly back north to First and Howard, where the makers of Claude work in the glass building that used to be Slack's headquarters.
params.fact: In 2026 Anthropic leased all 25 stories of 300 Howard Street, one of the largest office commitments in San Francisco history.

title: Oracle Park
blurb: 24 Willie Mays Plaza, San Francisco, CA 94107

params.clue: Time for a ball game: fly southeast to the red brick ballpark on the bay where home runs splash into the water, and land on the field.
params.fact: The right field wall is 24 feet high in honor of Willie Mays, who wore number 24.

params.clue: Cross the channel south into Mission Bay and find the glass tower Uber built, now home to the makers of ChatGPT.
params.fact: By March 2026 OpenAI's San Francisco offices passed one million square feet, all of it in Mission Bay.

params.clue: Keep flying south along Third Street to the old shipyard at Pier 70, where the accelerator behind Airbnb, Dropbox and Stripe meets in a red brick 1896 office on 20th Street.
params.fact: YC's main building was the office of the Union Iron Works shipyard, built in 1896 of brick and concrete and strong enough to survive the 1906 earthquake and fire.

params.clue: One of that accelerator's most famous alumni began by renting out air mattresses. Fly northwest to its headquarters, an old battery factory beside the freeway on Brannan Street.
params.fact: In 2008 the founders kept the company alive by raising $30,000 selling breakfast cereal named after the two presidential candidates.

title: San Francisco City Hall
blurb: 1 Dr. Carlton B. Goodlett Pl, San Francisco, CA 94102

params.clue: Keep heading northwest to the Civic Center and land beside the gold-trimmed dome that rises higher than the US Capitol's.
params.fact: Joe DiMaggio and Marilyn Monroe were married here in January 1954.

title: Twin Peaks
blurb: Christmas Tree Point, Twin Peaks Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94114

params.clue: Climb southwest to the two grassy summits in the middle of the city and land at the lookout with a view of nearly every stop you have visited.
params.fact: The summits are one of the few remaining homes of the endangered Mission blue butterfly.

title: Painted Ladies
blurb: Steiner St between Hayes St and Grove St, facing Alamo Square, San Francisco, CA 94117

params.clue: Fly north-northeast down to Alamo Square, where a row of Victorian houses poses in front of the skyline, just like on TV, and thread the ring in front of them.
params.fact: The row has appeared in an estimated 70 movies, TV shows and ads, including the opening credits of Full House.

params.clue: Head north-northwest to the Marina and find the Roman-looking rotunda beside a lagoon, built for the 1915 world's fair, and land on its dome.
params.fact: From 1934 to 1942 its exhibit hall held eighteen lighted tennis courts.

title: Golden Gate Bridge
blurb: Golden Gate Bridge, US-101, San Francisco, CA 94129

params.clue: For the grand finale, fly northwest to the orange suspension bridge across the strait and fly through the ring hanging under its deck at mid-span.
params.fact: When it opened in 1937 it had the longest suspension span in the world, a record it held until 1964.
